faqs.a:
(a)
Definitions.
As used in this section:
(1)
Obstruct
means to render a passageway impassable or make passage thereupon unreasonably inconvenient
               or hazardous; to place furniture or other personal property upon a passageway unless
               incidental to the lawful use of the passageway; to stop or stand within or occupy
               a crosswalk for a period of time longer than that reasonably necessary to cross over
               the roadway, except when necessary to avoid conflict with vehicular traffic, or in
               compliance with the direction of a police officer or an official traffic control device;
               or to cause a violation of other applicable law, such as the Americans with Disabilities
               Act, to occur or exist the passageway.
(2)
Passageway
means an alley, building entrance, public elevator or entrance to a public elevator,
               sidewalk, stairway, stairwell or stairwell landing, railway, creek, creek bank or
               other waterway, or any other public place used for the passage of persons, vehicles,
               or conveyances.
(3)
Person with authority to control the use of the premises
means a uniformed peace officer, emergency medical technician, paramedic, firefighter,
               or city employee acting within the course and scope of their duties.
(4)
Public place
means property owned by the city or other political subdivision of the State.
(b)
Unlawful act.
No person shall intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly:
(1)
Obstruct a passageway, whether the obstruction was created by the person acting alone
               or with others; or
(2)
Disobey a reasonable request or order to end or discontinue an obstruction of a passageway
               that is issued by a person with authority to control the use of the premises to maintain
               public safety.
(c)
Exception.
Subsection (b)(1) shall not apply to an obstruction caused by a medical emergency,
               or by attending a parade, festival, performance, rally, demonstration, meeting, or
               similar event conducted in the public right-of-way pursuant to any permit or license
               issued by the city, or as otherwise authorized by law.
(d)
Penalty.
Any violation of this section shall be punished by a fine or imprisonment not to
               exceed the limits established in
section 1-5
of this Code.
(Ord. No.
4838
, § 2, 3-20-2023)
